chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh and Ibrahim the sons of Nusayr, from al-Ubaydi, from Hisham ibn Ibrahim al-Khatli, who is al-Mashraqi, who said:

Abu al-Hasan al-Khurasani (peace be upon him) said to me: What do you say regarding Istita'ah (capacity) after Yunus? Do you follow the opinion of Zurara? And the opinion of Zurara is wrong! I said: No, but — may my father and mother be ransomed for you — what do you say about Istita'ah? As for the opinion of Zurara regarding the one who is given capacity, we disassociate from it as it is not of the religion of your forefathers. And the others believe in pre-destination (al-Jabr), and we disassociate from it as it is not of the religion of your forefathers. He said: Then with what do you say? I said: With the saying of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). And he asked about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And to Allah is due the pilgrimage of the House for whoever has the capacity to find a way to it' — what is his 'capacity'? He said: So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: His health and his wealth. So we take according to the verdict of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) spoke the truth, this is the truth.

key_terms.زرارة: Zurara ibn A'yan, a prominent companion of the Imams

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of Istita'ah (capacity) for Hajj according to the Imams?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kashi’s Rijal highlights the theological debate on 'Istita'ah' (capacity) for Hajj, where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) corrects Zurara’s specific view and rejects the extremes of Jabr (compulsion) and Ikhtiyar (free will) by defining capacity as the combination of physical health and financial wealth. This clarification anchors the jurisprudential requirement of ability in tangible, objective conditions rather than abstract theological determinism, reflecting the Ahl al-Bayt’s balanced approach to divine decree and human agency. The Imam’s affirmation validates this definition as the authentic understanding derived from the Prophet and the Imams, distinguishing it from other scholarly opinions.

en.ammaar-muslim: 11. [11/167] Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh and Ibrahim the sons of Nusayr from al-Ubaydi from Hisham b. Ibrahim al-Khatli [al-Mashraqi] who said:

Abu al-Hasan al-Khurasani عليه السلام said to me: what do you say regarding Istita`a after Yunus? Do you subscribe to the opinion of Zurara while the opinion of Zurara is wrong! I said: no, rather – may my father and mother be ransomed for you – [we subscribe to] what you say about Istita`a. As for the opinion of Zurara about the one who is given capacity then we disassociate from it as it is not of the religion of your forefathers. Others believe in pre-destination which we similarly disassociate from as it is not of the religion of your forefathers. He said: what then do you say? I said: we affirm the view of Abi Abdillah عليه السلام when he was asked about the words of Allah Mighty and Majestic “and pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed by Allah to the people – for whoever has the capacity to find a way to it” [3:97] – what is his ‘capacity’? so Abu Abdillah عليه السلام said: good-health and having wealth, so we subscribe to the verdict of Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, he said: Abu Abdillah عليه السلام spoke the truth, this is how it is.
